opening: I want to understand agent sandboxes from the kernel up to CubeSandbox, SPACE and E2B runtime. I know Go, Rust and C, and E2B's API; I don't know KVM or virtio. The three checkouts are already in your repos/ — use those copies, don't clone them again.

learner.background: Systems engineer, eight years of Go, Rust and C in production; comfortable with Linux processes, namespaces, cgroups and containers. I have used E2B's API from a client but never read its runtime, and I know neither KVM nor virtio beyond the names.

answers.goal: I need to design our own agent sandbox: boot untrusted code fast, snapshot and restore it, and know which layer does what across CubeSandbox, SPACE and E2B runtime.
answers.level: Go, Rust and C are fine; KVM, virtio and the guest kernel side are new to me.
answers.background: Eight years of systems work in Go, Rust and C; I know Linux processes, namespaces, cgroups and containers. I have called E2B's API but not read its runtime. KVM and virtio are just names to me.
answers.time: An hour a day for a week; I want to be reading something first-hand within the first few minutes.
answers.language: English is fine; keep the original terms.
answers.scope: From the kernel boundary up: KVM and virtio, microVM boot, then how CubeSandbox, SPACE and E2B runtime snapshot and restore. Skip the web consoles and billing.
answers.depth: Follow the call paths through the code and pin the lines; I want to read the specs where the code relies on them.

probe: Where does CubeSandbox actually enter the guest kernel during a launch, and what does the KVM side do there? Point me at the code or the spec line.
